# Changelog — Darts

## 0.6.2

- When a member removes their DevQuake account, what they added to your things (comments, items, ticks, photos…) stays, shown as “REMOVED_…” instead of their name.

## 0.6.1

- “Back” links now return to the page you came from, with its filters and where you had scrolled to.

## 0.6.0

- The app’s card on DevQuake and its front page now show how many members use it and its totals: finished games, tournaments.

0.5.2

- People who do not use the app yet now see what it does on its front page, with a link to the user manual, and shared links show the app’s own picture.

## 0.5.1

- The section you are in (Start, Practice, Casual, Tournaments, Statistics, Profile) is now marked in the tabs under the title.

## 0.5.0

- Score progress: every game, and every match of a tournament, shows visit by visit what each player threw and their score after it, with a chart of how the scores went. Search a player’s name to see only their visits, a summary of how they scored, and whom they played.

## 0.4.0

- A short notification now confirms what you did: the game or tournament was created, the settings, board or profile were saved, a round started, a link was copied, and so on.
- Deleting or removing something now asks in the app’s own window, which says what will happen, instead of the browser’s pop-up.

## 0.3.0

- Every option of a new game or tournament now explains what your choice means: the start score, double in, double/single/master out, legs, the Cricket variant, rounds, lives and the drill settings.

## 0.2.0

- See what you have left as you enter each dart: the scoreboard and a “Left” box update straight away, and in Cricket your marks fill in dart by dart.
- The send button now says what happens: “Next: Ana”, “Next visit”, “Bust · next: Ana”, “Win the leg” or “Win the game!”; until all darts are in, it tells you how many are still missing.
- A trophy celebration when a game is won.
- A faster keypad: one tap per dart with Double and Treble keys, keyboard shortcuts on a computer, and one-click visits with the finishes, your own frequent visits and common scores at that point of the game.
- The screen no longer jumps while you enter darts: messages and suggestions keep their place.

## 0.1.1

- Clearer suggestions while you play: “Where to aim next” names every dart in words (for example Treble 20 → Double 20, or 7 in any ring), shows whether to throw them in order, and says in a sentence what each one does, such as which score it finishes or which number comes next.

## 0.1.0

- Set up your darts profile: your name at the board, throwing hand, level, how you enter scores and your favourite double.
- Practise alone with 501/301, Cricket, Shanghai, Around the Clock, Count-Up, or target and finishing drills; every visit and its three darts are kept.
- Play casual games with friends who join by code or QR code: the host starts the game and can remove a player so someone else can join. Killer for up to 8 players.
- Enter darts by tapping the dartboard or with a keypad (+ / −, single, double, treble). Every dart is checked with the rules, and up to three suggestions show the finish or targets that bring you closest to winning.
- Run tournaments on your boards: each board has its own QR code, players are placed on boards, the app suggests who plays whom by strength and you can swap players. Entry fee, your share and who paid are tracked, and the bracket updates live.
- Watch any match live with its link, without being able to change the score.
- Your own statistics: results per mode, every opponent, average, best visits and finishes, where your darts land, the scores you throw most, and your strong and weak skills, with practice drills made for your weak spots.
